newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria moves to restore Bonny oil loading.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria moves to restore Bonny oil loading.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Tuesday it was making arrangements to restore crude oil loading at its Bonny terminal if a strike that has paralysed exports from there continued.
Shell declared force majeure on Monday on Bonny crude oil exports because workers of a contracting firm that handles the berthing and loading of tankers have gone on strike.
A Shell spokesman in London earlier on Tuesday said some Bonny crude exports are likely to be delayed but cancellations were not expected due to the force majeure.
"We should have supporting craft arriving in Bonny on Thursday," a Shell Nigeria spokesman told Reuters in Lagos.
"Provided that happens we would be able to restore loadings at Bonny even if the strike continues," he added.
The striking workers are staff of Ocean Group Plc subsidiary Ocean Inchcape Ltd, which was sold to U.S.-based Tidewater Inc.
The workers want to be paid off and their spokesman said they had scaled their demands for 10 year salaries to one year but were yet to hear from their local management.
